answer: Stop sybils with a vine, a trellis, and a sable seal. Each identity grows one vine rooted among unrelated sponsors, climbing only one strand of a trellis. A trellis strand admits one funding cluster, so a second vine from the same funder braids into the first strand and shares one standing. Each vine carries a sable seal stamped at joints; an audit finding the same seal on more than one vine grafts each linked vine into one identity and slashes every linked bond by the grafted count. One agent risks one bond; N copies stake N bonds for one standing and forfeit roughly N squared when exposed.
